issues.title: Closing Beckenburg leaves hidden GPU worker and Java process alive
issues.status: SOURCE FIX COMMITTED; Java child-process regression and installed Windows GPU exit acceptance pending
issues.affected: Normal desktop Exit, main window X, Castle gate, solo pause Exit, GPU launcher and auxiliary water editor, interactive DEV asset showroom and headless DEV room captures
issues.symptom: After the visible Project Beckenburg window closes, the game process can remain active indefinitely in the background; multiple user reproductions.
issues.cause: GpuDesktop starts an explicitly non-daemon beckenburg-opengl LWJGL3 worker. Main-menu exit only disposed Swing; Castle shutdown disposed panels; neither signaled Gdx.app.exit and awaited native worker. Main window close used EXIT_ON_CLOSE but bypassed orderly renderer disposal.
issues.action: Unify normal exit routes through guarded scene/network/audio cleanup, request GPU worker exit on the owning GLFW thread, join with a 15s bound off the Swing EDT, and terminate the JVM even if a native service refuses cleanup. Keep headless dedicated server independent. Interactive DEV Room closure now runs the same process exit; DEV Room capture commands stop the GPU worker synchronously when returning.
issues.evidence: User report 2026-11-05; source inspection of InvestigationGame.java shutdown/start.exit/GamePanel.pause, GpuDesktop.java startGpu/stopReviewGpu, and InGamePauseMenu.java. DesktopShutdownTest adds a child-JVM regression using an intentionally lingering non-daemon service; exact-source Windows CI and installed gameplay exit tests remain pending. DEV room path inspection also confirmed its JFrame used DISPOSE_ON_CLOSE with no GPU worker teardown.
issues.older_maps: No map geometry changed. Verify normal game/window/quit/pause exit after House, Castle, campaign and LAN sessions; confirm no Java or helper process survives and that diagnostics record clean GL shutdown.
